item.content:encoded:
In our October Land Use Meeting, we met Joe McKay from the Lowe’s Property Group to talk about SUGARGROVE. This will be built on the former Snelgrove’s parcel. It is between Commonwealth and 2100 South, and 800 East and 900 East, where Snelgrove used to be, and to the west of the bank on the SW corner of 2100 East.

Here are the slides showing where they are in figuring out the layout of this project. We will see this again when they figure out where the signs will go.

The City Council has been discussing EXPANDING HOUSING OPTIONS.  The Council discussed potential alterations to the proposal, including requiring homeownership for at last one unit on the property.  After discussing Council Members’ concerns and significant public outreach two public hearings have been scheduled for Tuesday November 10, and Tuesday November 17. Also, a postcard will be sent to every residential parcel in the city. We will provide more details closer to those dates.

For our November Land Use meeting at 6 p.m. at Sprague Library, we will be discussing GEM Sugar House. This is for the parcel that is now Zion’s Bank.  The bank will be torn down, and rebuilt on the first floor of an apartment building.  Here are the details of that proposal. There may be changes to the project as a result of the Planning Commission meeting, and we will update this if we get the information. This is what the Planning Commission was discussing:

  • Approve the conditional use ordinance allowing Sugar House Business District Drive-thru(Denied)
  • Affordable Housing Incentives Administrative Design Review process (Approved)
  • Unobstructed open space (Denied)

Commissioner, staff, and Applicants discussed the following topics • • Affordable Housing Incentives Administrative Design Review process • Unobstructed open space

item.content:encoded:
SHCC LUZ REPORT 2026 OCTOBER

We have learned that the GEM Sugar House project ( Zions Bank) will begin deconstruction in late September or Early October.

The Expanding Housing Options is slowing down. The city is beginning to realize that few people even know about this, and most comments are negative, so they will send a postcard to every residential property owner and seek more media attention so people start to understand the EHO. 

We had the planner Aaron Barlow come to the SHCC meeting an hour before the September meeting, and he talked about  Planned Development and Community Benefits, and showed his slides, and answered questions.  We got 32 people on line for that, plus however many came early for SHCC and heard the talk. Here is a link to his talk and the slides. Two changes being proposed are both Development Ordinances.

Sarah explained the distinction between the two proposed planning tools:

•  Transfer of Development Rights: Focused on environmental conservation (e.g., near the Great Salt Lake) rather than historical preservation in Sugar House. It allows owners to monetize land by selling development potential to other areas like Granary.

•  Transfer of Building Rights: Part of the Planned Development Community Benefit Ordinance, this allows transferring height within a single parcel (up to 50%) to create varied streetscapes. This would apply only to specific zones like MU (Mixed Use).

Community Engagement

Sarah Young addressed concerns regarding recent comments made by the City Council chair about public participation levels. She emphasized that the Sugar House Community Council remains highly active and encouraged residents to provide constructive feedback rather than just negative remarks on platforms like Nextdoor. The discussion touched on systemic barriers to engagement, such as language gaps and meeting schedules, which affect overall civic participation.

Please continue to send me comments about Expanding Housing Options or Planned Developments and Community Benefits. Why allow extra height if the community doesn’t get anything for it.?

The next SHCC Land Use and Zoning Committee meeting will be October 19 at 6 p.m. at Sprague Library.

Zions wanted to modify a requirement for unobstructed open space. To meet the goals, the plan had to have at least 10% of the lot be open […]

The post SHCC LUZ REPORT 2026 SEPTEMBER first appeared on Sugar House Community Council.
item.content:encoded:
In August, the Planning Commission voted to allow a GEM SALT LAKE Zions Bank drive-thru at 2200 Highland Drive, in a 16-floor building, but didn’t like that it didn’t meet open space requirements. Zions wanted to modify a requirement for unobstructed open space. To meet the goals, the plan had to have at least 10% of the lot be open space area, “any area of a lot which is completely free and unobstructed from any structure or parking area.” The current plans had only 2% in unobstructed open space. The applicants wanted to count the fifth floor of the building, which had a deck and pool, to be counted. The top floor had another 1700 feet of unobstructed open space. Zions had changed the unit count, and some units that were originally labeled “short-term rental” were now being called “hotel units”. The total count would be 139 residential units and 52 hotel units. The zoning requirements clearly said the open space had to be on the ground floor. The commission voted to deny the modification to the open space requirement.

The other issue for Zions was the Affordable Housing Incentives. The units were to be deeply affordable, and to people who are at 30% AMI. This will be determined administratively later. If they meet that requirement, they will get two extra floors of height (not three).

We also discussed the Planned Development Amendment and Community Benefit Requirements proposal.The city is trying to divide projects into things that staff can deal with administratively, or things that need Planning Commission review. We have a lot of confusion about what the language in this proposal means, and only a few of us had attended the planning briefing. The planner, Aaron Barlow, has agreed to meet at the Neighborhood Hive (2065 E 2100 S) from 6-7 p.m. on September 2, right before the SHCC meeting from 7-9 p.m. He will have slides and give a presentation and then answer your questions as time permits. If you want to watch it on YouTube go to YouTube and look for Sugar House Community Council. I know some of you have already given me your questions, if you haven’t, send an email to judi.short@gmail.com. He would like the questions ahead of time so he can be prepared. After the meeting, I want your feedback on the proposal, I might write a second letter.

The last item on the agenda was Expanding Housing Options. This will be going to the City Council shortly. Here is a link if you want to refresh your memory. You can see the letter I sent to the Planning Commission at the link. Peter Wetzel, pwetzel@sbcglobal.net, talked about his thoughts. These changes will apply to every residentially zoned parcel in the city. You can write a letter to the Planning Commission. Peter has written an Op Ed that appeared in the August 26th edition of the Tribune on Page A7.

The next SHCC LUZ meeting will be September 21 at 6 p.m. at Sprague Library. We don’t have any new proposals yet, but you know SLC Planning, they won’t forget us!

item.content:encoded:
Mayor Erin Mendenhall has initiated a petition to amend Section 21A.55 of Salt Lake City’s Zoning Ordinance to update the procedures and requirements for Planned Development Petitions. This will create two tiers of review:

  • Minor Planned Developments (Staff Level approvals)
  • Major Planned Developments (Planning Commission Approvals.

Here is a link to the proposal: www.slc.gov/planning/2026/07/21/openhouse2026-00611/

Please note: When you look at the city document, you will come to a series of 3/4″ blue lines. Click on each line to reveal the content, these contains a lot of the key information for understanding this change to the zoning code.

After you have read the document, please fill out the form and give us your comments. The comments will go with our letter to the Planning Commission about this proposal.

item.content:encoded:
We discussed the Gem Sugar House, the former DI Parcel on Highland Drive, and the Parkway parcel between 1300 E and 17th East, along I-80.

  • GEM Sugar House (Zions Bank) Here is a link to the project on our website with some drawings and explanation of what they would like to do. The parcel is zoned MU-11, which can be a maximum of 125 feet. Buildings that want higher than 85 feet must go through design review.
  • This means the building can be up to 125 feet in height, with taller buildings (up to 11 floors) allowed through the design review process. To get to 182 feet, which they are asking for, they have to comply with the ordinance. Here is a link to the details of the zoning ordinance for MU -I I.
  • We are writing a letter to the Planning Commission, which will show up on the GEM Sugar House page on our website when it is finished,.  This is our first foray into the MU-11 zone, which is quite a bit taller than we have ever had. If you want to make a comment, you can do so up until a week before the Planning Commission meeting , which will be August 12. You can read the comments we already have on the GEM Sugar House page and use the comment form if you wish to comment.

We had a discussion about the RFP for the former DI property. We do not know much about what they plan to do with the parcel.  We would like to see some affordable housing units, and perhaps some community benefits, like a daycare center or Senior Center (a space that has both might be fun). Maybe commuter items like fresh flowers, magazines, snacks, etc.  We would like to see parking provided because not everyone will take the streetcar. Maybe a parking structure with some cool murals, a small fee even to be used to maintain it?  I know there is a potential for parking by the TCBY sometime in the future. Maybe this is the most practical and will help the businesses get customers to the area?

We also discussed the parcel between Parkway Avenue and I-80 owned by South Salt Lake City, This originally was a piece of Sugar House Park. Neighbors on Parkway have been using some of it for gardens and other uses. South Salt Lake is now planning to fence it off so the Parkway neighbors will no longer have any access. South Salt Lake will build a tall fence along the parcel. South Salt Lake purchased that property in the 1970’s and has two underground water tanks on the property and are adding two more.

item.content:encoded:
We received the GEM SUGAR HOUSE proposal, which is the redo of Zions Bank on the first floor of a 16-story apartment building. Here is a link to the proposal, where you will find all the information provided by the applicant. The Zoning is MU-11. It will have 195 apartments with 9,000 square feet of commercial on the first floor. They are asking for a Conditional Use and Planned Development approvals to allow a drive-through use and modifications to the required open space. There are separate applications to be reviewed administratively for Design Review and Affordable Housing Incentives, and Lot Consolidation.  These decisions for Design Review and Affordable Housing Incentives will be made after the Planning Commission decision. Our letter to the Planning Commission is due July  27, so please read through all the details and use the form to give me your comments.

For your information, the City Council has been working on the SUGAR HOUSE SPECIAL ASSESSMENT AREA.This would be in the core commercial area focused on economic promotion applied to all eligible properties within the designated boundaries. A second assessment would apply to properties with frontage on certain streets for specialty lighting and signage.

Please read through all the documents. It will not go the Planning Commission. This will give the business district the ability to have extra things, like Holiday lights, and pay for help to do the maintenance.

567 East Warnock is another project, with four townhomes.  They are asking for a rezone to RMF-35. When you read through the information, you will see references to the two other townhome buildings that are right in that area.  One is finished, the second one is under construction. sugarhousecouncil.org/articles/current-petitions/567-e-warnock-ave-rezone-to-rmf-35/  Please fill out the comment form.

At the construction meeting, we learned that the S -Line Extension is beginning. Demolition at the old DI Site.  Work on the rail line will begin in mid-July at McClelland Street crossing, with some preparation at the parking lot on the Sugar House Center. Here is the map of the route. The businesses around the area, Highland Drive and Sugar House Center, etc have been informed about the construction.  There will be communication throughout the construction to make sure their concerns are met.

Fairmont Heights, 10th and Elm, are under construction, and the GEM Sugar House won’t start until after the first of the year.

item.content:encoded:
The City Council has been working on a Sugar House Special Assessment Area for Sugar House. This would be in the core commercial area focused on economic promotion applied to all eligible properties within the designated boundaries. A second assessment would apply to properties with frontage on certain streets for specialty lighting and signage.

There are three documents you should read to understand how this works. The idea is that the commercial stores and the property owners will be assessed a fee. The area covered is identified in the Council Staff Report. The details are in these documents, and none of this is approved yet. It is estimated this will start in early 2027 for three years. There is a period where those being assessed can provide comments and protest the details.

The full tentative timeline for establishing the SAA is on pages 10-11 of the administrative transmittal. It is also included as a separate attachment (Attachment A) to this staff report.

item.content:encoded:
We have received a petition to rezone the property at 567 E Warnock Ave from R-1/7000 Single Family Residential to RMF-35 Moderate Density Multi-Family Residential. You will see by the maps that this is just south of I-80, where we approved several similar projects in 2022. The Planning Commission recently approved an alley vacation on the west side of this parcel, and this has now gone to City Council for final approval. The developer plans to put four townhome units on this parcel. This will be incorporated into the Woodland Commons Townhome development west of the site. One of the two buildings is complete, and the second is under construction.

Here is the letter we received from the city. And, here is the letter sent by the developer. You will find a picture of what the development will look like, a map of the immediate area so you can see how it fits in with the other two townhome developments approved a few years ago, and the alley vacation, which is currently in process. This will be on the LUZ agenda June 15 at 6 p.m. at Sprague Library. We have until July 11 to get our comments in to the city.
